description: Roll a saving throw: d20 against the character's Physical, Evasion, Mental, or Luck save, succeeding on a roll equal to or above the score. Call it when an effect threatens the character and the rules allow a save. A failure is recorded; apply what it costs yourself.

name.description: The name of the character making the save.

stat.description: Which save: save_physical for bodily harm, save_evasion for dodging, save_mental for willpower, save_luck for blind chance.

reason.description: What the save is against, in a few words.

modifier.description: A situational bonus to the save, negative for a penalty, such as -the attacker's combat skill on an execution attack or a poison's -2.

description: Ask the player to roll a saving throw for their own character, then record the d20 they rolled against the character's Physical, Evasion, Mental, or Luck save. Use it instead of roll_save for the player character: the player presses the roll button and the result is final. A failure is recorded; apply what it costs yourself. A returned reaction has already been applied by the engine; narrate its outcome rather than asking the player to roll again for it.

player_input.details: {save} save against {cause}: roll 1d20 and meet or beat your save score.

character.description: The name of the player character making the save.

save.description: Which save: physical for bodily harm, evasion for dodging, mental for willpower, luck for blind chance.

cause.description: What the save is against, in a few words.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to roll, such as 'Roll a Physical save against the poison.'

modifier.description: A situational bonus to the save, negative for a penalty, such as -the attacker's combat skill on an execution attack or a poison's -2.

description: Use the Empowered Sorcery art to reroll a variable die in a spell's effect, such as its damage dice. Pass the spell's dice and the total already rolled; the caster may choose either total. If the caster is the player character, ask the player before calling this; an NPC's choice is the GM's. Record the Effort commitment separately.

dice.description: The variable dice to reroll, such as 3d6.

original.description: The total the spell already rolled.

character.description: The caster; leave out for the player character, or name an NPC with the art.

description: Use the Inexorable Effect art after an enemy succeeds on a save: reroll that save and use the new result, which is the worse outcome for the enemy. The art is once per scene and requires the caster to have it. If the caster is the player character, ask the player before calling this; an NPC's choice is the GM's. Record the Effort commitment separately.

target.description: The enemy whose successful save is being rerolled.

reason.description: What the save was against, in a few words.

character.description: The caster; leave out for the player character, or name an NPC with the art.

description: Roll 2d6 for the first reaction of an NPC or group the party meets, adding the greeting character's Charisma modifier when a player character can greet them. The higher the total, the friendlier the reaction. Use it whenever the party meets a creature or group unless bloodshed is certain, and describe the mood to the players before they act.

character.description: The player character greeting the NPC, for the Charisma modifier. Any player character if none greets them.

greeting.description: Whether a player character is in a position to greet the targets, which adds their Charisma modifier.

cause.description: Who or what the party has met.

description: Check an NPC's Instinct: roll 1d10 against the Instinct score printed in its statblock. A roll no higher than the score means the creature acts on impulse rather than its best judgment. Player characters never check Instinct.

name.description: The name of the NPC whose instincts are tested.

instinct.description: The creature's Instinct score from its statblock.

cause.description: What tempts the creature to act on impulse.

patch.description: Roll on one or more of the rule set's dice tables and log every result. Use the world-generation tables (significant_terrain, terrain_quirk, terrain_antagonists, nation_disputes_with_neighbor, ruler_class, government_struggle, history_event, community_tags, court_tags, ruin_tags, wilderness_tags) to build the starting region. Also available: site_type, site_feature, site_hazard, site_enigma, site_treasure, deeps_type, ruin_characteristic, ruin_encounter_human, ruin_encounter_beast, ruin_encounter_sapient, encounter_template, wilderness_event, dungeon_event, monster_shape, monster_drive, and monster_twist. Use dungeon_reaction (2d6) for a quick reaction, or roll_reaction to add Charisma. The engine returns the results; you decide what they mean.

description: Travel overland by the WWN rules. A day is ten hours of marching; base speed is 3 mph on plains, 2 in light forest or desert, 1.5 in dense forest or rugged hills, 1 in swamp, and 0.5 in mountains or broken highland. A road doubles the pace, foul weather halves it, and deep snow reduces it to a tenth. The engine moves the character and advances the clock. Apply the returned food, water, firewood, and privation figures with use_item, add_strain, and the usual bookkeeping; foraging takes half a day and a Wis/Survive check at the returned difficulty.

road.description: True when the route follows a road, which doubles the pace.

weather.description: Foul weather halves the pace; deep snow reduces it to a tenth.

description: Roll initiative for each side of the encounter: 1d8 plus the best Dexterity modifier in the side, with ties going to the party. Call it once every participant has joined and before the first turn, so the narration can use the result. A side then acts as a block in that order, and a late joiner joins their side's block. No player character makes an individual initiative roll.
Start an encounter on a map. Create the map first if the place has none. Add the participants, then call roll_initiative before anyone acts.

map.description: The name of the encounter map where the fight happens.

description: End the encounter in progress once the fight, chase, or parley is over.
Add a character to the encounter on a side. Player characters default to the party and NPCs to the foes.

name.description: The name of the character joining the encounter.

side.description: The side they fight on, such as party or foes. Leave it out for the usual side.

description: Take a character out of the encounter, such as one who flees or is left behind.

name.description: The name of the character leaving the encounter.

description: Make an NPC's attack: d20 plus its attack bonus against the target's Armor Class, with a natural 1 always missing and a natural 20 always hitting. The engine rolls the damage; on a miss it still applies the attack's Shock when the target's AC is low enough, but a thrown or ranged attack never inflicts Shock. Pass damage_modifier or shock_modifier for a Focus or magic bonus the engine does not compute itself. An attack is refused unless the attacker is the character taking their turn, so the player presses Start for the NPC's turn first; pass force true only for an action the story needs outside the turn order, such as an ambush. On the encounter map, the attack must be within its melee reach or ranged band, with a clear line of sight; a reach weapon such as a pike can strike 10 feet away. Move the attacker with place_participant first when it is refused for distance.

attack.description: The name of one of its attacks, as the statblock lists it.

hit_modifier.description: A situational bonus or penalty to the hit roll: -2 long range, -4 firing while meleed or attacking prone, -1 dual wielding, -2 or -4 cover, -2 for total defence.

damage_modifier.description: A bonus or penalty to the damage roll from a Focus, magic, or the situation that the engine does not compute itself. It is added after the attack's dice and attribute.

shock_modifier.description: A bonus or penalty to the attack's Shock from a Focus or magic that explicitly reaches Shock. It never applies to a thrown or ranged attack.

count.description: How many attacks to resolve. Leave it out to use the statblock's attacks per action, or set 1 for a single attack.

description: Ask the player to roll their attack with a carried weapon or unarmed, then record the d20. The player rolls only the d20: the engine adds the weapon skill, the best weapon attribute, and the attack bonus to the hit; it adds the attribute and a Warrior's Killing Blow to weapon damage; and it applies Shock on a miss when the target's AC is low enough, with Shock taking the attribute but not other damage bonuses. A thrown or ranged attack never inflicts Shock. Pass damage_modifier or shock_modifier for a Focus or magic bonus the engine does not compute itself, such as Armsmaster's Stab level added to damage or Shock. Use it for the player character; the player presses the roll button and the result is final. An attack is refused unless the player character is taking their turn; their turn starts automatically when it comes up. When the player orders a different character to attack, such as a hireling, and it is not that character's turn, do not call this tool for them: say plainly that the character holds until their turn, and resolve the attack when their turn comes. Pass force true only for an action the story needs outside the turn order. On the encounter map, the weapon's melee reach or ranged band and a clear line of sight are enforced: pass range_band for a ranged shot, or leave it out to let the engine choose the band for the distance.

player_input.details: {weapon} against {target}: roll 1d20 only. The engine adds your attack bonus and weapon modifiers, then rolls damage.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

weapon.description: The carried weapon's name, as given, or unarmed.

hit_modifier.description: A situational bonus or penalty to the hit roll: -2 long range, -4 firing while meleed or attacking prone, -1 dual wielding, -2 or -4 cover, -2 for total defence.

damage_modifier.description: A bonus or penalty to the damage roll from a Focus or magic that the engine does not compute itself, such as Armsmaster's Stab level. It is added after the weapon's dice and attribute.

shock_modifier.description: A bonus or penalty to Shock from a Focus or magic that explicitly reaches Shock, such as Shocking Assault's +2. It never applies to a thrown or ranged attack.

range_band.description: Optional. The range band the shot is fired at. Short has no penalty; long gives -2 to hit. Leave it out to let the engine choose the band for the distance on an encounter map. A shot beyond the weapon's long range is refused.

dual_wield.description: True when attacking with two one-handed melee weapons. The engine applies the rule set's dual-wield hit penalty and damage bonus.

prompt.description: What the player is asked to roll, such as 'Roll your attack with the long sword.'

description: Resolve several NPC attacks on one character at once, such as a creature's several attacks per action or several foes striking the same target. Each attack rolls its own attack die and applies its own damage in turn. Every attacker must be taking their turn unless force is true. On the encounter map, each attack must be within its melee reach or ranged band, with a clear line of sight; move its attacker with place_participant first when it is refused for distance.
Harm a character outside combat, from a fall, poison, exposure, or privation. Use harm from an attack only through attack or player_attack. A PC brought to 0 HP is mortally wounded; an NPC is dead.

stat.description: The stat harmed. Outside combat, usually hp.

description: Restore lost points of a stat, usually hit points, from a healing spell, art, or item. It never restores more than the character has lost. Recovering a mortally wounded character is a separate act.

Stop a mortally wounded character's dying clock. The character wakes with 1 hit point after ten minutes and gains the Frail condition. In the book this needs an Int/Heal or Dex/Heal check at difficulty 8 plus the rounds since they fell; call roll_check first and stabilize only on a success. Set force true only when the story requires the aid to work without that check.

explanation.description: How they were stabilized, such as a tourniquet or a healer's care.

description: Clear a mortally wounded character's dying state, or wake a character knocked out by a nonlethal blow, leaving the harm they took for heal_character to restore. Use it after the character is stabilized and the healing magic or rest reaches them. It works on a player character or an important NPC.
Pass the player's own d20 roll for a save the engine has marked due after harm. Use it only when a save is owed.
Take a character out of the fight. Set safe to true only when the character has a clear route away.

Record one party rest. Every player character recovers: a night restores hit points equal to their level, one point of System Strain, all spell castings, and scene and day Effort. A few moments restores scene Effort only. A week of bed rest restores hit points equal to seven times their level, seven points of System Strain, all castings, and ends Frail with medical care. The rest moves the clock once. Frail characters recover no hit points or Strain from a single night.

length.description: moments for a short break, night for a full night's rest, extended for a week of bed rest.

interrupted.description: True when something breaks the rest, which then counts as moments only.

patch.description: Move the campaign clock forward when time passes in the fiction. Use hours for a short wait or exploration time (six 10-minute turns make an hour), and parts only for a clear block of the day or a night. Do not advance time for a conversation, a few actions, or an NPC leaving the scene; the narration covers that.

Hire a retainer into a player character's company. The retainer has a rolled sheet like an NPC's and is controlled by the player. Its wage is paid in silver from the employer each new day, and an employer who cannot pay is reported as unpaid. Leave personality, accent, or quirks out to have them rolled. Names must be unique among locations and characters. The retainer joins with enough experience to catch up to the employer's level, and the player makes its level-up choices on the character sheet. To hire an NPC already in the story as a retainer, use hire_existing_npc.

employer.description: The player character paying the wage.

wage.description: Silver per day, zero or more.

patch.description: Turn an NPC already in the story into a retainer in a player character's company. The NPC keeps their name, description, personality, accent, quirks, pronouns, and summary; choose character options that fit how they have been portrayed, including a class from their work and skills and Foci from what they have shown. The NPC must be an NPC, able to act, out of an encounter, and at the employer's location. The employer must be a player character with a location. The retainer is controlled by the player, and its wage is paid in silver from the employer each new day. It joins with enough experience to catch up to the employer's level, and the player makes its level-up choices on the character sheet. Give the wage the NPC asks for.

Change a retainer's daily wage in silver, including to 0 when they now serve without pay. Use this when the employer and retainer agree to new terms or the story changes what is paid. The character must be a retainer.

wage.description: Silver per day, zero or more.

patch.description: Remove a retainer from its employer's company. It stays where it is and becomes an ordinary NPC.

cause.description: Why the retainer leaves, in a few words.

patch.description: Give a character an item they are given, find, or loot, with no payment. A catalogue item takes its listed size, uses, and damage; a new item needs its size and, for a weapon, its damage dice. Never use it because the player says the character has something or reaches for it: check the inventory first, and if the character does not carry it, say so and let them find, buy, or do without it. Never use it for something the character pays for; use buy_item.

damage.description: The weapon's damage dice, such as 1d8. Leave it out for gear.

size.description: How much of the inventory it fills. Leave it out for a catalogue item.

patch.description: Remove an item from a character's inventory. Dropping equipped armor or a wielded shield also unequips it and recalculates Armor Class.

description: Ready a carried item for use, or stow it. A character can keep only half their Strength in slots readied; readied weapons can attack. Readying armor or a shield does not equip it; use equip_armor to wear or wield it. Stowing equipped defense also unequips it. Retrieving a stowed item takes a Main action.

ready.description: True to ready it, false to stow it.

description: Wear or remove a carried, readied suit of armor, or wield or stop wielding a carried, readied shield. Only one suit and one shield can be equipped; equipping another replaces that slot. Armor Class and shield protection against Shock update automatically. The returned Armor Class is authoritative: wearing armor or wielding a shield can lower it when a feature such as the Vowed's Unarmored Defense works only without that equipment. Consult the character's features before explaining a change.

item.description: The carried armor or shield's catalogue name.

equipped.description: True to wear or wield it, false to remove it.

description: Begin a long-running effort and track its points toward a target: a personal project, a piece of research, a magic working, or another long effort. The kind and goal are free text; the target is how many points of work it needs. Advance it with advance_project as time, money, and rolls are spent. Use add_faction_asset and take_faction_turn for factions instead.

kind.description: What sort of effort it is, such as project, research, working, or faction.

description: Add progress to a project, research effort, magic working, or another long effort. Record in the note what the time, money, or roll bought. The project completes when progress reaches its target.
Give up a project, research effort, magic working, or another long effort.
List every project, research effort, and magic working with its progress, notes, and whether it is complete or abandoned.

Give a faction one of the rule set's assets, such as Infantry, Smugglers, or Farmers. The kind may be the asset's id or its book name. Its cost, hit points, Magic, Attack, Counter, and qualities are resolved from the rule set. An asset can act once per faction turn.

kind.description: The asset kind's id or book name, such as infantry or Infantry.

name.description: A display name for this copy of the asset, unique within the faction. Defaults to the book name.

notes.description: An optional note, such as where the asset is based.

description: Change a faction asset's display name, qualities, or notes. A note is appended to the asset's record. Use damage_faction_asset and repair_faction_asset for hit points.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

notes.description: A note to append to the asset's record.

qualities.description: The asset's full quality list, such as ["Subtle", "Special"].

description: Remove or destroy one of a faction's assets.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

description: Record that a faction asset used its action for the current faction turn. An asset can act only once per turn; the tool refuses a second action. End the turn with take_faction_turn to ready every asset again.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

note.description: What the asset did, such as attacking, moving, or repairing.

description: Reduce a faction asset's hit points by an amount. Hit points stop at zero rather than going negative.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

description: Restore a faction asset's hit points by an amount. Hit points stop at the asset's maximum.

asset.description: The asset's name or id within the faction.

description: Close a faction's current turn and begin the next one. Every asset is ready to act again. Use this after resolving the faction's actions, upkeep, and asset abilities.

note.description: What the faction accomplished this turn.

patch.description: Buy an object a character keeps, with silver. A catalogue item costs its listed price; for anything else, give both a price and the item's size. Use buy_service for a room, meal, passage, toll, or other service that is not carried. Armor updates the buyer's Armor Class automatically.

price.description: The price in silver for an item not in the catalogue.

patch.description: Buy a service for one or more characters: a room, meal, passage, toll, bribe, or anything else that is not carried away. A listed service uses its listed price and effect, so leave price out. For any other service, give a price you set from similar services. The first character named pays for the whole service. A service never adds an inventory item.

price.description: The price in silver for a service the marketplace does not list. Leave it out for a listed service.

patch.description: Find items and services the marketplace sells, by name or category.

description: Create a creature from the bestiary and place it at a location. Give the template id (use search_monster to find it) and any changes to its stats, armor, or attacks.

rules.description: Rule ids attached to the creature, whose text the GM sees while it is present.

patch.description: Find bestiary statblocks by name or description.

description: Spend an art pick on an art of the character's own tradition. Class charts grant art picks at levels 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 for a full mage, and at levels 2, 3, 6, and 9 for a partial mage (3, 6, and 9 for a partial Necromancer or Elementalist).

art.description: The feature id of the art.

description: Spend skill points on a permanent +1 to one attribute. The first boost costs 1 point, the second 2, and so on to 5, at minimum character levels 2, 2, 3, 6, and 9; a character may buy five in total.
Give a character starting money instead of an equipment package: roll 3d6 and multiply by 10 silver pieces, as the book allows. Use it once at creation and do not also grant a package.
Make a square grid map for an encounter at a location, such as a ford, room, or yard. A map is needed before start_encounter can be used.

template.description: An optional encounter map template id.

palette.description: A map palette id from map_options: parchment, stone, forest, sea, ember, frost, shadow, or royal.

background_color.description: A hex colour for the board's ground.

grid_color.description: A hex colour for the board's grid lines.

description: Change an encounter map's name, location, description, size, look, or extend it on any side. Extending keeps every mark and token, shifting them by the cells added to the left or top.

palette.description: A map palette id from map_options. Leave out to keep it.

ambient.description: An ambient look id from map_options. Leave out to keep it.

extend_left.description: Add columns on the left; existing marks and tokens shift right.

extend_up.description: Add rows at the top; existing marks and tokens shift down.

description: Delete an encounter map that is no longer needed.
Put an encounter participant on a cell of the map grid.

Spend one use of a consumable the character carries. Lighting a torch spends one torch and gives six ten-minute turns of light; filling and lighting a lantern spends one pint of oil and gives twenty-four. The lantern itself is not consumed. A day's food and water are eaten by the engine when the party rests; call this for a torch, oil, or another deliberate use.
